Man ordered to pay £78,614 under Proceeds of Crime Act for illegal tree felling

14 June 2024

A man who made tens of thousands of pounds from illegally felling ancient woodland has been ordered to hand over his criminal profits.

Thomas Jeffrey Lane, 45, of Pontypool, appeared at Swansea Crown Court on 14 June 2024 for a Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA) confiscation hearing.

Lane had previously been convicted in January 2024 of illegal tree felling after clearing approximately 8 hectares of protected ancient woodland near Abergavenny without a licence. He had sold the timber for an estimated £95,000.

At the original sentencing hearing, Lane received an 18-month suspended sentence and was ordered to carry out 200 hours of unpaid work.

Following a financial investigation by NRW and Gwent Police, Lane was brought back to court for POCA proceedings.

The court determined that Lane's benefit from criminal conduct was £78,614 and that his available assets were sufficient to meet a confiscation order for this amount.

Her Honour Judge Margaret Jones ordered Lane to pay £78,614 within three months or face an additional two years imprisonment.

NRW's Head of Enforcement said: "This case demonstrates that we will use all available legal tools to ensure that environmental criminals do not profit from their illegal activities. The Proceeds of Crime Act is a powerful deterrent."

The offences were committed contrary to Section 17 of the Forestry Act 1967.
